summary: Phase F4.3 Persistent Print Status backend — 10/10 pytest assertions PASSED against the live preview backend. All scenarios A (basic mark/persist/unmark + printed_at audit stamp survives unmark), B (idempotency + printed_at refresh on re-mark, unmark twice), C (tracking-ID guard: 422 on mark without tracking; 200 on unmark; 200 after tracking added), D (404 for unknown id and cross-tenant scoping via user2), E (regression: list surfaces new fields, POST defaults print_status:'', PUT /shipments doesn't touch print_status, DELETE on Printed row still 200) — all green.
action_items: None — Phase F4.3 backend is production-ready. Main agent can mark the task working:true and proceed to frontend integration if not already done.
critical_code_review_comments: print_status router (/app/backend/routers/print_status.py) is small, well-documented, and correctly reuses server.py's db + get_current_user via lazy init(). Tracking-ID guard mirrors F4.2 semantics correctly (accepts either tracking_id OR manual_tracking_id, both stripped).
printed_at audit trail preserved on unmark (deliberate — verified by A4).
Cross-tenant safety: user2 gets 404 (not 403) on admin's shipment id — correct, since {id, user_id} filter matches zero docs.
Shipment Pydantic model in server.py exposes print_status and printed_at as Optional[str]='' so GET /api/shipments returns the persisted state without breaking older clients.
seed_data_creation: 6 TEST_F43_* shipments created during the run; all deleted (soft-delete via DELETE /api/shipments/{id} returning 200) in test finally blocks. No dangling state.
